newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa earnings drop due to strike, lower prices.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa earnings drop due to strike, lower prices.

text.p: Aluminum Co. of America, blaming special charges, lower prices and a strike at one of its plants, Friday posted much lower-than-expected third-quarter earnings.
The world's largest aluminum producer posted earnings of $133.9 million, or 77 cents per share, on an operating basis. That fell well below Wall Street expectations of 95 cents per share.
Alcoa earned $226.4 million, or $1.27 per share, in last year's third quarter. Revenues fell slightly this year to $3.2 billion from $3.3 billion last year.
Including a $65.5 million restructuring charge, Alcoa posted net income of $68.4 million for the quarter, or 39 cents per share.
Alcoa blamed the lower earnings on the charge plus a 22-day strike by the United Auto Workers union at its forging plant in Cleveland.
Alcoa also said lower aluminum prices hurt earnings. The company adjusts its customer contracts to correspond with current aluminum prices.
Aluminum prices have been declining in recent months and dropped sharply during September.
Alcoa stock fell as much as $2.25 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange before ending down 37.5 cents at $60.
Analysts said they were mildly disappointed but not surprised by the earnings.
"If anything, I thought that maybe earnings would come in on the disappointing side," said Tom VanLeeuwen at CS First Boston. "Industry conditions have been difficult."
VanLeeuwen said aluminum inventories on the London Metal Exchange have continued to rise while aluminum prices have fallen. "Inventories and prices have an inverse relationship," he said.
Alcoa surprised some analysts by posting a quarterly loss of $6.8 million at its Brazilian operation, an equity partnership plant.
"That plant should be making money," said Chuck Bradford at UBS Securities. "It made $7 million in the second quarter."
A company spokeswoman said the loss at the plant was caused by lower aluminum ingot prices in the global market, lower fabrication prices in the Brazilian market and higher costs.
For the first nine months of 1996, Alcoa earned $484.3 million, or $2.77 per share, before after-tax charges of $105.5 million. After charges, net income was $378.8 million, or $2.16 per share.
In the first nine months of 1995 the company earned $639.6 million, or $3.58 per share.
